title: No source gives S1 a table for the payoff, the settlement range or the floor
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.6); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-006 Data); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-01, R9)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; CON s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13
description: The calculation produces a payoff, a range and a floor, and no source says where the result is held. The ownership rows give S1 no table at all; TSD S1 T3.1 declares only the tables valuation and score, neither of which carries a payoff, a range bound or a floor; the legacy data table names v_ace_account (P1), treatment (S2), decision_log_entry (P7) and rule_row (P7), none of which is this service's. The two stories therefore hold the result as the outcome of the local decision record and as elements of the route answer, and declare no calculation table and no migration.
evidence: Context pack S1 ownership rows show Tables (0) - None; TSD S1 T3.1 lists valuation (DF-COL-018 to DF-COL-027, DF-COL-043 and DF-COL-044) and score (DF-DEC-019 to DF-DEC-027) and no payoff, range or floor object; the legacy RWB-E4-006 Data table lists v_ace_account, treatment, decision_log_entry and rule_row; FSD S1 A2.6 names no data object of its own.
area: Data model and schema, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner and the ACE DB owner
proposed: The service owner confirms whether a calculation result table is needed; if it is, the DB story of S1 creates it in its own Flyway sequence and RWB-S1-E4006-CON declares its elements in a minor version, with no change to this behaviour.

title: The operation names of the account, freshness and rule-set reads are not published
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T5.2, T5.3); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.6.2 integration points); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R9)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s12.9 Call-type summary; CON s3 Preconditions; s12.2; s12.8; s12.9
description: The step consumes five rows across four owners and no source publishes the operation name of any of them: the account and balance data product of rwb-source-data, the freshness read of the same owner, the rule-set-in-force and decision-log read of rwb-decision, the case and account-set read of rwb-case, and the authorise operation of rwb-access. TSD S1 T5.2 describes the cross-module calls as published Java interfaces and T5.1 is the row None. Both stories build against a documented use, a placeholder and a fake, and invent no path, parameter or transport.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack give S1 three REST operations of its own and name no consumed operation; TSD S1 T-A.1 lists API-S1-001 only; TSD S1 T5.1 is None and T5.2 names Java interfaces; FSD S1 A2.6.2 names the integration points as ALS and GL and the Rules component and gives no operation name.
owner_role: P1 rwb-source-data owner, P7 rwb-decision owner, P3 rwb-case owner and P4 rwb-access owner
proposed: Each owner publishes the operation name of its row before the wave 3 tag, and RWB-S1-E4006-CON replaces the placeholder with the published name in a minor version; the client adapters change and the behaviour does not.

title: The source of the balances and the composition of the payoff disagree between sources and the formula is not published
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.6.1, A2.6.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-SET-01); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-006 story and AC1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md (E4 S1 FEAT-VAL-06 row); Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and Physical Schema v6 (DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-022, DF-ACE-024)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s4 Flow; s8 Business rules; s11 Data; CON s11 Data
description: Three sources describe the same read in two ways. FSD S1 A2.6 and R-SET-01 say the payoff is calculated from ALS, the legacy story and AC1 say the balances are read from v_ace_account, and the Epics 3 to 8 Specification reconciles them as the ALS balances read through v_ace_account. No source publishes the composition of the payoff out of total_balance, past_due_amount and collections_fee, the treatment of the collections fee, or the rounding, although AC1 gives the three amounts. The stories read the balances at the ACE batch date and take the composition as a governed value with a version, and invent no arithmetic.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.6.1 and A2.6.2: Works out the payoff from ALS and the settlement range from the rules; R-SET-01: Calculate the payoff from ALS and set the range from reference data; legacy RWB-E4-006 story: The payoff is read from v_ace_account at the ACE batch date and the range from rule_row; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 line E4 S1 FEAT-VAL-06: the ALS balances read through v_ace_account; AC1 gives total balance 1240000, past due amount 86000 and collections fee 4500 with no formula.
area: Business rules and data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: Business owner of the settlement route set and the S1 service owner
proposed: The business owner publishes the payoff formula, its fee inclusion and its rounding as a governed value with a version, and the business analyst confirms that v_ace_account is the single source after the ACE re-base; the story then reads the formula and changes no code.

title: The freshness limit of the payoff, the range bounds and the floor method are not published
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-SET-01, R-SET-02, R-SET-03, R-SET-04, R-SET-05, R-SET-25); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.6.3.1 BR-S1-006); Recovery Workbench Decision Log v10 (S1 package phasing)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow; s8 Business rules; s12.2; CON s3 Preconditions; s8 Business rules; s11 Data; s12.1
description: The routing workbook names the conditions and the outcomes but not their values: the freshness limit that makes payoff_as_at stale at R-SET-03, the range bounds that R-SET-04 tests against an offer, the floor_price of R-SET-05, and the field that holds the range when R-SET-25 fires for a missing payoff or floor. BR-S1-006 forbids writing any such value in code, so the stories read them with their rule id and version and declare no number, and the settlement route set is the only place they can come from.
evidence: R-SET-02 conditions on payoff_as_at inside the freshness limit and R-SET-03 on payoff_as_at older than the freshness limit, with no limit value published; R-SET-04 uses settlement_range_low and settlement_range_high and R-SET-05 floor_price with no values; R-SET-25 fires when the payoff or the floor price is missing and names no field; FSD S1 A2.6.3.1 BR-S1-006 requires every changeable value to be read from reference data with its version.
area: Business rules and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: Business owner of the settlement route set and P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: The settlement route set is published with its freshness limit, its range bounds, its floor method and the missing-value names, and both stories read them at their version; a change of value is a rule release and not a build.

title: The trigger set of the calculation names an event, a timer and a batch and no source publishes any of them
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.6.2 step 1); _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1: Events 0, Jobs 0); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-006 AC1)
section: APP s4 Flow; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.6 Schedules; CON s12.4; s12.6
description: FSD S1 A2.6.2 step 1 gives the step three possible triggers, a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer, and publishes no event name, no Schedule and no job for any of them; the ownership rows give S1 no event and no job. Legacy AC1 instead starts the calculation when the case owner prepares the route decision. The stories run the calculation inside the route-decision command, prove the batch leg through the freshness rule VR-S1-006-1, and declare no subscription and no Schedule.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.6.2 step 1: Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer; context pack S1 ownership rows: Events (0) - None and Jobs (0) - None; legacy RWB-E4-006 AC1: When the case owner prepares the route decision.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner and the Temporal platform owner (RWB-PLT-E1071)
proposed: If a batch-completion trigger is needed, the S1 owner declares a Temporal Schedule in RWB-PLT-E1071 and this story adds the trigger signal; the calculation itself is unchanged.

title: The element name of the payoff amount and the contract shape of the calculation elements are not published
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-SET-02, R-SET-04, R-SET-05); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-006 Endpoints)
section: APP s12.1 REST operations provided; CON s12.1 REST operations provided; s13
description: TSD S1 T-A.2 gives RouteRequest in and Approval out with no field list, and the legacy Endpoints table gives one operation with no body. The names payoff_as_at, settlement_range_low, settlement_range_high and floor_price come from the routing workbook and are used as declared elements; the element name of the payoff amount itself appears in no source. The baseline declares the four workbook names, carries the placeholder for the payoff amount element and declares no invented wrapper object.
evidence: TSD S1 T-A.2: Request RouteRequest, Response Approval, with no element table; legacy RWB-E4-006 Endpoints: POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/route with no body; R-SET-02 uses payoff_as_at, R-SET-04 uses settlement_range_low and settlement_range_high, R-SET-05 uses floor_price; no source names an element for the payoff itself.
proposed: The service owner confirms the element names at the RWB-S1-E4006-CON tag; a confirmed name replaces the placeholder in a minor version with no behaviour change.
